owner_decision: #2 (2026-11-06): prepare safe fix (Windows repro test + process-authority impact + regression plan); do NOT patch the frozen kernel before the plan is tabled.
finding: aisef2/app/client.py:46 (_is_gone) probes liveness with a bare os.kill(pid, 0) documented as 'no signal is ever sent'; that contract is false on Windows, where os.kill(pid, 0) is destructive or raises, never a safe probe.

windows_semantics.mechanism: signal.CTRL_C_EVENT==0 -> console-control branch; CPython<=3.12 falls through to OpenProcess+TerminateProcess(handle,0) (exit code 0); CPython>=3.14/3.13-post-fix delivers a real Ctrl+C or raises OSError. Never a liveness probe in any deployed version.
citations: CPython gh-58689 / GH-128932 / GH-128937 (3.13 os.kill error-handling fix)

aisef2_signal0: aisef2/app/client.py:46 (the only signal-0 probe in aisef2/)
v1_legacy_already_safe: aisef/control/state.py:73 (POSIX fallback only; Windows uses OpenProcess/GetExitCodeProcess)

reachability_on_windows.guarantee: _is_gone runs only inside `except RangeEscaped`; Windows uses the _Job backend whose escaped() returns [] unconditionally (process_range.py:277-278, KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE + no BREAKAWAY_OK :250), so flight.escaped is always empty, RangeEscaped (:534) is never raised, and left_the_range()==[] triggers `if not left: raise` (client.py:68-69) before any _is_gone call.
reachability_on_windows.adversarial_refute_unreachable: FAILED to refute; corrected mechanism: unreachability comes from the hardcoded [] in _Job.escaped(), not the OS no-breakaway flag.
caveats: Cygwin/MSYS2 Python (os.name=='posix') reaches it via _Posix, but os.kill(pid,0) is a genuine safe POSIX probe there.

Tests call client._is_gone directly with os.kill mocked (tests/v2/test_v21_pl7_session_teardown.py:98-136); the real-process variant is @skipUnless(linux) (:179). No test exercises real Windows _is_gone.

authority_impact.view: kernel controller view during session release; pid controller-derived, not subject-named
authority_impact.clause2_independent_controller_view: letter-level breach IF reachable (os.kill(pid,0) ledgered as a READ / LIVENESS_PROBE_SIGNAL_0 but on Windows is an unledgered terminate; pid-reuse guard skipped because process_table() raises on Windows)
authority_impact.severity_given_unreachability: LOW / LATENT — invariant holds in shipped product; defense-in-depth defect resting on cross-module coincidence (_Job.escaped()==[])

why_ci_green: client.py:46 has no destructive_sites.json ledger row, so whole-tree da.check(ROOT) would FAIL — but the two whole-tree assertions are @sealing-gated (sealing_gate.py GATED :30,:32), skipped on branch/PR CI. Inconsistency: sealing_gate.py:10-13 says live-tree static checks must NOT be gated. Also the LIVENESS_PROBE_SIGNAL_0 class passes on argument shape only (no platform dimension), so it is the wrong guard anyway.

safe_fix.option_a: Route the _is_gone fallback through a Windows-safe existence check (pid_alive pattern: OpenProcess(PROCESS_QUERY_LIMITED_INFORMATION)+GetExitCodeProcess==259). `return not pid_alive(pid)`. POSIX byte-identical; makes the docstring true on all platforms. Owner question: aisef2-native helper vs importing V1 aisef.control.state.pid_alive.
safe_fix.option_b: POSIX-gate the probe (`if os.name!='posix': return False`). Minimal; less complete.

windows_repro_test.asserts: @skipUnless(win32): a real live child survives client._is_gone (fails on unfixed Windows), and _is_gone returns False for a live process
windows_repro_test.validated_off_windows: imports clean, self-skips on darwin (1 skipped)
